title: The Curse That Came True That Night
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2.57-58 (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.63-64)

captions.instagram:
Part 2 of 2. King Dasharatha died of grief for his son, as a curse had said. In Valmiki's Ramayana (Critical Edition, Ayodhya 2.58), Dasharatha carried the young ascetic's water pot to his blind parents' ashram and told them the truth himself. The sage said: had you not told me yourself, your head would have split; because it was done unknowingly, you live. The son appeared in divine form, said he had won a great state by serving his parents, and rose to heaven. Then the father spoke the curse: "As I grieve for my son, so you too will die of grief for a son." Years later, on the night Dasharatha told this story to Kausalya, at that same midnight, he died. Both tellings are told with devotion.

Did you know the son rose to heaven in Valmiki's telling? Tell us 👇 Jai Shri Ram!

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2.57-58 (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.63-64)

captions.youtube_description:
Part 2 of 2. King Dasharatha died of grief for his son, as a curse had said. In Valmiki's Ramayana (Critical Edition, Ayodhya 2.58), Dasharatha carried the young ascetic's water pot to his blind parents' ashram and told them the truth himself. The sage said: had you not told me yourself, your head would have split; because it was done unknowingly, you live. The son appeared in divine form, said he had won a great state by serving his parents, and rose to heaven. Then the father spoke the curse: "As I grieve for my son, so you too will die of grief for a son." Years later, on the night Dasharatha told this story to Kausalya, at that same midnight, he died. Both tellings are told with devotion.

Did you know the son rose to heaven in Valmiki's telling? Tell us 👇 Jai Shri Ram!

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2.57-58 (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.63-64)
Verses:
• He asks Dasharatha to tell his father and to pull out the arrow; Dasharatha does, and he dies — 2.57.34-39
• Hunting at night on the Sarayu he heard a sound like a pot filling, took it for an elephant and shot at the sound — 2.57.14-17; 2.58.13
• Dasharatha tells the story himself, to Kausalya, at midnight, remembering his old misdeed — 2.57.3
• The blind father: 'Son, why are you late? Bring the water quickly'; 'you are the eyes of the blind' — 2.58.5; 2.58.8
• Sage: had you not told me yourself your head would have split in a hundred thousand pieces; because it was unknowing, you live — 2.58.19; 2.58.21
• After the water offering the son appears in divine form, says he won a great state by serving them, and rises to heaven in a vimana — 2.58.39-42
• The curse: you too will die of grief for a son — 2.58.46
• That night, after midnight, Dasharatha dies crying 'O Raghava' — 2.58.56-57
• The young man is never named in Valmiki: only तापस / तपस्विन् / मुनिपुत्र / 'your son' (whole of CE 2.57-58 read; parents unnamed too) — 2.57-58 (whole episode)
